text.p: Troubled German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG said on Tuesday it had pared net losses by over 100 million marks in the first four months of its 1996/97 business year from a previous deficit of 250 million marks.
Babcock, which recently hired a new chief executive, also said its incoming orders and order book were stable. Turnover edged up slightly between October and the end of January.
Group incoming orders were unchanged at 2.8 billion marks, with order books flat at 11.4 billion marks. Turnover was up to 1.9 billion marks from 1.8 billion.
Deutsche Babcock's workforce was down 13 percent to 29,303.

The company hired Klaus Lederer to replace chief executive Heyo Schmiedeknecht, who stepped down in January following an acquisition spree which dragged the group to a net loss last year of 434 million marks and bank strained credit lines.
The company was due to hold a news conference at 0900 GMT.
